assessment.label: Security configuration score
assessment.disclaimer: This is a weighted checklist of observed public security configuration, not a percentage probability that the website is secure. Even 100/100 does not establish that a site is safe or free of vulnerabilities.
methodology: Version configuration-v1 uses fixed, heuristic weights totaling 100 points; they are not a standardized or independently validated security rating.
A passed checklist check earns its weight. CSP and framing observations earn presence credit only; directive strength and effective restrictions are not validated.
Unavailable or missing checks remain unassessed. Their weights produce a possible range, rather than being treated as failures or removed from the denominator.
Coverage is the percentage of checklist weight that was assessed. The upper end of a partial range assumes every unassessed check would earn its weight.
Domain registration age, DNS addresses, page title, mobile viewport, language and image descriptions do not change this security configuration score.
No authentication, application logic, exploitation, malicious content or complete TLS/cipher audit is performed. AI cannot change the measured findings or scoring rules.

rating.label: Needs review
rating.summary: Security observations need review. Open the priority findings to see the evidence and next steps.
rating.methodology: With complete checklist evidence, 80–100 points starts green, 50–79 amber, and below 50 red. Any recorded security issue prevents green. A certificate verification issue, unencrypted final page, or a password form using HTTP or GET makes the light red, even with a high score. Incomplete evidence stays neutral unless one of those priority issues was observed. Extra form and cookie checks do not change the numeric score. These are project-defined review priorities, not a safety verdict.

ai.summary: This synthetic sample represents a public website homepage. Its encrypted connection checks passed, but the page includes an HTTP script reference and lacks some browser policies. Start with the resource reference, then review the content and framing policies. These configuration observations do not establish whether an attack is possible.

items.explanation: No enforcing Content Security Policy was observed in the synthetic page's header or markup.
items.why_it_matters: A Content Security Policy gives the browser rules about which resources, including scripts, the page may load. A carefully designed policy can reduce some script-injection risks, so it is useful to review this setting.
items.next_step: For the site owner: list the page's required resources and evaluate a policy in report-only mode before enforcement.
items.limitation: Missing this policy does not prove an exploitable flaw; application inputs and script behavior were not tested.

items.explanation: The synthetic HTTPS page references a script using an HTTP URL.
items.why_it_matters: HTTP does not encrypt that resource's transport. Browsers may block or upgrade the request, so the reference is worth correcting and checking in a real browser.
items.next_step: For the site owner: replace the reference with an HTTPS resource, then verify the page still works.
items.limitation: The scan does not execute the page and cannot establish what a visitor's browser actually loads.

items.explanation: No supported framing restriction was observed in the synthetic response.
items.why_it_matters: Framing rules let the site control which pages may embed it. Restricting unwanted embedding can help reduce deceptive overlay scenarios, while some sites intentionally support embedding.
items.next_step: For the site owner: identify legitimate embedding needs before choosing a frame-ancestors policy.
items.limitation: This observation does not establish actual browser behavior or the feasibility of an attack.
